name: JADE
tagline: New Zealand's integrated object database, language and app server for building line-of-business systems.
description: JADE, from Christchurch-based Jade Software Corporation, is an all-in-one platform: a Pascal/Modula-2 flavoured object-oriented language, an IDE and debugger, an application server and a transactional object database, so classes are persisted directly without an ORM. It first shipped in 1996 and still runs long-lived systems in logistics, rail freight, finance and government, mostly in New Zealand, Australia and the UK. The current release series is Jade 2025, which adds Orb (HTML-over-the-wire web apps), Direct REST, .NET (not just .NET Framework) support and an event stream producer; Synchronized Database Service keeps standby copies for high availability. It is a sound choice if you already have JADE skills or systems, but a hard sell for greenfield work given its small talent pool.

license.name: Proprietary (free development licence; paid deployment licences)

pricing.notes: A free, limited development licence is available; production deployments pay licence fees per process/server.

scale.notes: Single primary database; Synchronized Database Service maintains secondary copies for failover and read offload.

strengths: Language, app server and object database in one stack; no ORM layer
Persistent objects and collections with full ACID transactions
Decades of production use in logistics, rail and finance systems
Synchronized Database Service for standby copies and failover
weaknesses: Proprietary language and runtime with a small developer pool
Strong lock-in: data and logic are tied to the JADE platform
Little presence in modern cloud, container or open-source tooling
useCases: Maintaining and extending existing JADE line-of-business systems
Domain-rich business applications modeled as persistent objects
Organisations in NZ/Australia with in-house JADE expertise
notIdealFor: Greenfield projects needing a large hiring pool
